original_sentence: FALMONT—On 17 March, 476 students and 36 teachers at Falmont Primary School escaped an earthquake that hit the county at 2:27 p.m.
readingExamples: FALMONT—On 17 March, 476 students and 36 teachers at Falmont Primary School escaped an earthquake that hit the county at 2:27 p.m.
definitionEn:
(1) n. an area of a country or state that has its own local government, and is larger than a city or town
(2) n. (in the US) one of the areas that a state is divided into for the purposes of local government
(3) adj. of, relating to, or characteristic of a county, especially its administration or its sports teams

definitionEn:
(1) n. a sudden event such as a flood, storm, or earthquake that causes great damage, loss, or suffering
(2) n. something that has a very bad result or effect; a total failure

definitionEn:
(1) phr. (after a noun) as a whole; in general (e.g. society at large)

(3) phr. at length; fully and in detail (formal, e.g. to speak on a topic at large)

definitionEn:

(2) n. a bad physical response of the body to a drug, food, or other substance
(3) n. a chemical change that happens when two or more substances are put together

definitionEn:

(2) n. a series of actions done in a certain order or manner to achieve a particular result

definitionEn:

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (情绪)涌动,充溢
uncommonMeanings.example: Laughter bubbled up from the back of the classroom, uncontrollable and infectious, until even the strict old teacher could not keep the corners of his mouth from twitching. （读后续写·课堂·情绪蔓延）

posExamples.sentence: The little boy pressed his nose against the cold glass, watching a single silver bubble rise slowly through the fish tank, and for one perfect moment the noise of the crowded aquarium seemed to fade away. （读后续写·童趣·凝神观察）

I am writing to remind fellow students that this charity fair is not merely a soap bubble of good intentions, but a lasting effort that will bring real relief to children in flood-hit areas. （应用文·倡议书）
As the two friends finally reunited at the airport gate, a joy that had been building for years bubbled over into tears, and they held each other without a single word. （读后续写·重逢·情感爆发）
History repeatedly warns us that every speculative bubble, whether in property or technology, eventually bursts, leaving behind those who mistook rising numbers for lasting value. （议论文·理性与狂热）

idioms.translation: 戳破某人的幻想;使美梦破灭
idioms.example: I hated to burst her bubble, but I gently reminded her that talent alone, without years of quiet practice, rarely blossoms into greatness. （读后续写·忠告·打破幻想）
When the bubble finally burst and the investors vanished overnight, the young entrepreneur learned the hardest lesson of all: hope built on hype cannot survive reality. （议论文·投机的代价）

collocations.example: On that warm spring afternoon, the children blew bubbles across the playground, each fragile sphere catching the sunlight before drifting apart in the breeze. （读后续写·童年·画面感）
Her dream of studying abroad had once seemed as delicate as a soap bubble, ready to vanish at the slightest touch of doubt. （读后续写·梦想·脆弱）
The diver noticed an air bubble escaping from his mask and forced himself to keep his head and rise slowly to the surface. （读后续写·潜水·危机）
Economists had long warned that the property bubble could not keep inflating forever, yet few chose to listen. （议论文·经济·警示）
Anger bubbled up inside him, but he clenched his fists and swallowed the harsh words that were burning on his tongue. （读后续写·忍耐·心理）
The whole team bubbled over with excitement as the final whistle confirmed their unlikely victory. （读后续写·比赛·狂喜）
One honest sentence from her mentor was enough to prick the bubble of complacency she had been floating in. （读后续写·点醒）

collocations.translation: 生活在与世隔绝的小世界里
collocations.example: Sheltered by wealthy parents, he had grown up in a bubble, utterly unaware of the hardships beyond his own comfortable street. （读后续写·成长·脱离现实）
The reunion dinner bubbled with laughter as old classmates traded stories they had not shared in a decade. （读后续写·聚会·温馨）

synonyms.example: A thin layer of froth clung to the rim of the cup as she lifted her morning coffee, still lost in thought. （读后续写·清晨·细节）
synonyms.usage: froth 多指液体表面成片的细密泡沫(啤酒、咖啡、海浪),偏物质层;bubble 强调单个可数气泡,也可喻指经济泡沫或情绪涌动

synonyms.example: The angry waves crashed against the rocks, throwing up white foam that hissed and vanished into the sand. （读后续写·海边·气势）
synonyms.usage: foam 指大量聚在一起的白色泡沫(海浪、灭火器、洗涤剂),质感更厚重;bubble 是构成 foam 的单个小泡

synonyms.example: The mountain stream gurgled cheerfully over the smooth stones, a sound that instantly washed away the travellers' fatigue. （读后续写·自然·听觉）
synonyms.usage: gurgle 专指液体流动/冒泡发出的汩汩声,是拟声动词;bubble 作动词时既可指冒泡这一动作,也可喻指情绪的涌动

advancedExpressions.expression: a warmth / joy bubbled up within sb., ...
advancedExpressions.example: A quiet warmth bubbled up within her chest, spreading outward until the cold room no longer felt cold at all. （用液体冒泡意象具象化抽象情感,续写情绪高潮段）

advancedExpressions.expression: let us not allow ... to remain a mere bubble of good intentions
advancedExpressions.example: Let us not allow our promise of a greener campus to remain a mere bubble of good intentions; instead, let every one of us turn words into daily action. （倡议信,以'泡沫'比喻空谈,增强号召力）

advancedExpressions.expression: however dazzling ... may appear, it is ultimately a bubble that ...
advancedExpressions.example: However dazzling instant online fame may appear, it is ultimately a bubble that bursts the moment substance is found wanting.

sentenceUpgrade.original: She was very happy and could not hide it.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: A happiness she could no longer contain bubbled up inside her, spilling into a laugh so bright and sudden that everyone around her turned to smile too. （读后续写·情绪外溢）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: bubble up 液体意象具象化情绪 + spilling into 现在分词表结果 + 环境反应(everyone turned to smile)侧面烘托

sentenceUpgrade.original: The economy grew fast but then collapsed.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: What had looked like unstoppable prosperity proved to be nothing more than a speculative bubble, and when it finally burst, it swept away in a single night the savings that families had painstakingly built over decades. （议论文·历史教训）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: What had looked like... proved to be 名词化对比结构 + speculative bubble 术语精准 + when it burst 时间状语强化戏剧性 + painstakingly built over decades 对比毁灭之速

original_sentence: It immediately occurred to her that these were signs of an approaching tsunami.
readingExamples: It immediately occurred to her that these were signs of an approaching tsunami.
definitionEn:
(1) vi. to happen, especially without being planned or expected
(2) vi. to exist or be found in a particular place, situation or among a group
(3) vi. (occur to sb.) to come into someone's mind suddenly, especially as a new idea or realization

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 存在于,出现于(某处/某群体中)
uncommonMeanings.example: This rare species of butterfly occurs only in a handful of untouched valleys, and each sighting felt to the young researcher like a message from a vanishing world. （读后续写·科考·珍稀）

posExamples.sentence: The accident occurred so suddenly that, before anyone could cry out, the cyclist had already swerved off the road and vanished into the roadside bushes. （读后续写·突发事件·画面感）
I am writing to report that a series of minor thefts has occurred in our dormitory this term, and I sincerely hope the school will take immediate measures to protect students' belongings. （应用文·反映情况信）
Genuine breakthroughs in science rarely occur by chance; more often, they emerge only after years of patient observation, repeated failure and stubborn refusal to give up. （议论文·科学与坚持）
It suddenly occurred to me, standing alone on the empty platform, that I had forgotten to say goodbye to the one person who mattered most. （读后续写·顿悟·遗憾）

collocations.example: It never occurred to her that the shy new classmate she had ignored would one day become her closest friend. （读后续写·友谊·始料未及）
The teacher explained that these minerals occur naturally in the rocks of the region, sparking a wave of curiosity across the classroom. （应用文·科普/说明）
Such acts of quiet kindness occur far more frequently than the gloomy headlines would have us believe. （议论文·人性向善）
Profound changes occurred in the once-sleepy village after the new road connected it to the outside world. （读后续写·乡村巨变）
When a natural disaster occurs, it is our collective calm and cooperation, not panic, that saves lives. （议论文·应对灾难）

collocations.phrase: occur to sb. to do sth
collocations.example: It did not occur to him to check the weather forecast, a small oversight that would soon leave him stranded in the storm. （读后续写·疏忽·铺垫）
This misunderstanding commonly occurs among beginners, so there is no reason to feel discouraged. （应用文·答疑/建议）
Should any problems occur during the trip, please do not hesitate to contact our guide at once. （应用文·通知/须知）

synonyms.example: Everything happened in a blur — the screech of tyres, a scream, and then a silence that seemed to last forever. （读后续写·车祸·瞬间）
synonyms.usage: happen 最口语、最常用,可指任何事件;occur 更正式、书面,常用于书信、说明文和'occur to sb.'这一固定结构中

synonyms.example: The annual charity concert will take place in the school auditorium next Friday evening. （应用文·通知）
synonyms.usage: take place 多指有计划、有安排的活动(会议、典礼、比赛);occur 和 happen 则常指意外、偶然发生的事

synonyms.example: Whenever conflicts arise within a team, honest communication is the surest way to resolve them. （议论文·团队合作）
synonyms.usage: arise 多与抽象事物(问题、机会、争端、需求)搭配,强调'由某原因引发';occur 适用范围更广,可指具体事件

advancedExpressions.expression: it suddenly occurred to sb. that ..., and in that instant ...
advancedExpressions.example: It suddenly occurred to him that the stranger's face was strangely familiar, and in that instant a forgotten memory came flooding back. （用 occur to 引出顿悟,in that instant 制造转折,续写推动情节）

advancedExpressions.expression: should ... occur, please ...
advancedExpressions.example: Should any emergency occur during the field trip, please remain calm and follow your team leader's instructions immediately. （倒装虚拟条件 should ... occur,通知/须知中显正式）

advancedExpressions.expression: such ... does not occur by accident; rather, it stems from ...
advancedExpressions.example: Such remarkable progress does not occur by accident; rather, it stems from a nation's steadfast investment in education over generations.

sentenceUpgrade.original: Suddenly she thought that she had left the door open.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It occurred to her with a jolt of alarm that she had left the front door wide open, and without a second thought she spun around and dashed back down the darkened stairs. （读后续写·惊觉·连贯动作）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It occurred to sb. that... 固定结构显地道 + with a jolt of alarm 名词短语状语渲染心理 + spun around and dashed 连续动词营造紧迫感

sentenceUpgrade.original: Accidents often happen when people are careless.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Statistics reveal a sobering truth: the overwhelming majority of traffic accidents occur not because of poor roads, but because of a single careless moment behind the wheel. （议论文·安全意识）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Statistics reveal a sobering truth 数据引入增强说服力 + occur 替换 happen 更书面 + not because... but because 平行对比锁定核心原因

original_sentence: It immediately occurred to her that these were signs of an approaching tsunami.
readingExamples: It immediately occurred to her that these were signs of an approaching tsunami.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. (occur to sb.) if a thought or idea occurs to you, it suddenly comes into your mind
(2) phr. often used to say that someone did NOT think of something (it never occurred to sb.), stressing an oversight or a surprising realization

posExamples.sentence: As she stared at the old photograph, it slowly occurred to her that the smiling woman in the faded corner was none other than her own grandmother as a young girl. （读后续写·旧照片·恍然）
I am writing to suggest an idea that occurred to me during last week's cleaning: we could set up a book-recycling corner so that unwanted textbooks reach students who truly need them. （应用文·建议信）
It rarely occurs to us how much we owe to the countless strangers whose quiet labour makes our comfortable lives possible. （议论文·感恩与责任）
It never occurred to the arrogant champion that a nameless newcomer could pose any threat — until the final buzzer proved him painfully wrong. （读后续写·骄兵·反转）

collocations.example: It occurred to me that I had never once thanked my parents for the sacrifices they made in silence. （读后续写·自省·愧疚）

collocations.phrase: it never occurred to sb. (that / to do)
collocations.example: It never occurred to him to ask for help, so proud was he of solving every problem alone. （读后续写·性格·倔强）

collocations.phrase: a thought / an idea occurs to sb.
collocations.example: A bold idea occurred to her, and her eyes lit up as a plan began to take shape. （读后续写·灵光乍现）
It suddenly occurred to me that the answer had been hidden in plain sight all along. （读后续写·顿悟）

collocations.phrase: did it ever occur to you that ...?
collocations.example: Did it ever occur to you that the classmate you laughed at might be fighting a battle you know nothing about? （议论文/演讲·反问·同理心）

collocations.phrase: it occurred to sb. to do sth
collocations.example: Only when the room fell silent did it occur to her to check whether the old man was still breathing. （读后续写·危急·反应）

synonyms.example: It struck her, all of a sudden, that the melody drifting from the window was the very lullaby her mother used to sing. （读后续写·记忆·触动）
synonyms.usage: strike sb. 比 occur to sb. 更突然、更有冲击力,常带情绪波澜;occur to sb. 语气较平和,可指任何念头浮现

synonyms.example: It gradually dawned on him that the 'stranger' who had helped him was the very man he had once wronged. （读后续写·真相·渐悟）
synonyms.usage: dawn on sb. 强调'逐渐、终于'明白某个真相,过程感强;occur to sb. 侧重念头'突然'冒出,不强调醒悟过程

synonyms.example: When asked to name a true hero, the first person who came to mind was my quiet, hardworking grandfather. （应用文/记叙·联想）
synonyms.usage: come to mind 中性,指某人/某事被回想起来,主语是被想到的内容;occur to sb. 的主语是想法,更强调'突然想通'

advancedExpressions.expression: it was then that it finally occurred to sb. that ...
advancedExpressions.example: It was then that it finally occurred to her that true courage was not the absence of fear, but the choice to act in spite of it. （强调句 it was then that + occur to,续写点题升华）

advancedExpressions.expression: it occurred to me that we might ...
advancedExpressions.example: It occurred to me that we might invite retired teachers to share their experiences, which would surely enrich our reading week. （用 occur to me 引出建议,语气谦逊得体）

advancedExpressions.expression: has it ever occurred to us that ...?
advancedExpressions.example: Has it ever occurred to us that the convenience we take for granted is quietly reshaping how we think, feel and relate to one another?

sentenceUpgrade.original: She suddenly realized that she had forgotten his birthday.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It occurred to her, with a sinking heart, that in the whirl of her own busy life she had completely forgotten his birthday — the one day he had been quietly looking forward to for weeks. （读后续写·愧疚·细节反衬）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It occurred to sb. that... 固定句型 + with a sinking heart 心理状语 + 破折号补充信息制造反差(他默默期待)

sentenceUpgrade.original: People don't often think about how lucky they are.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It seldom occurs to us, cocooned in the comfort of everyday routine, just how fortunate we are to wake each morning safe, healthy and free. （议论文·珍惜当下）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It seldom occurs to us... 否定副词前置显文采 + cocooned in the comfort 插入分词短语 + 三形容词收尾(safe, healthy and free)节奏铿锵

original_sentence: Sabrina was frightened, but she soon kept her head.
readingExamples: Sabrina was frightened, but she soon kept her head.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. to stay calm and think clearly in a difficult, frightening or confusing situation instead of panicking
(2) phr. (contrast: lose one's head) to remain in control of one's emotions and judgement under pressure

posExamples.sentence: When smoke suddenly filled the corridor, most of the passengers screamed and shoved, but the young flight attendant kept her head, calmly directing everyone toward the nearest exit. （读后续写·危机·临危不乱）
I would like to remind all members that, should any emergency arise during the hiking trip, the key to survival is to keep your head and follow the leader's instructions. （应用文·安全须知）
In moments of crisis, those who keep their heads and act with reason, rather than surrendering to panic, are the ones who ultimately lead others to safety. （议论文·理性的力量）
Though her hands were trembling and her heart pounded wildly, Sabrina forced herself to keep her head and count the seconds between each wave. （读后续写·海啸·自我克制）

idioms.example: The captain kept his head as the storm raged, issuing each order in a voice so steady that the frightened crew slowly calmed down. （读后续写·风暴·领导力）
The instant the fire alarm blared, he lost his head completely, running in circles while others quietly walked to the exits. （读后续写·对比·慌乱）
A good leader keeps a cool head even when everything around him seems to be falling apart. （议论文·领导力）

idioms.translation: 勉强维持;不被困难压垮
idioms.example: Working two part-time jobs, she barely kept her head above water, yet she never once complained in front of her children. （读后续写·艰辛·坚韧）

collocations.phrase: keep one's head in a crisis / an emergency
collocations.example: The ability to keep one's head in a crisis is worth more than any textbook knowledge. （议论文·能力·素养）
Somehow she managed to keep her head, dialling the emergency number with steady fingers while the room filled with smoke. （读后续写·火灾·冷静自救）

collocations.phrase: keep one's head and think clearly
collocations.example: He told himself to keep his head and think clearly, and only then did an escape route reveal itself. （读后续写·困境·自我对话）
What impressed the judges most was her ability to keep her head under pressure during the final round of the debate. （应用文/记叙·比赛）

collocations.phrase: keep one's head, no matter what
collocations.example: 'Keep your head, no matter what happens,' the old fisherman had once told him, and now, alone on the heaving sea, he clung to those words. （读后续写·海上·信念）

synonyms.example: Take a deep breath and stay calm; panic will only make the situation worse. （应用文·安抚/建议）
synonyms.usage: stay calm 最通用直白,指情绪上不慌乱;keep one's head 更强调在混乱中仍能清醒判断、正确行动,含'不失去理智'之意

synonyms.example: Even as the reporters fired hostile questions, the young scientist remained composed and answered each one with quiet confidence. （议论文/记叙·从容）
synonyms.usage: remain composed 偏正式书面,强调外表举止的从容得体;keep one's head 更口语化,突出思维的清醒,常用于紧急、危险场景

synonyms.example: Despite the unfair criticism, he kept his cool and let his results speak for themselves. （议论文·涵养）
synonyms.usage: keep one's cool 侧重控制愤怒、不冲动发作;keep one's head 侧重在危险或混乱中保持理智判断,两者可近义,但侧重点不同

advancedExpressions.expression: though ..., sb. forced herself to keep her head and ...
advancedExpressions.example: Though terror surged through every nerve, she forced herself to keep her head and scan the room for another way out. （让步状语 + force oneself to 体现意志,续写危机段刻画勇气）

advancedExpressions.expression: in the event of ..., the first thing to do is to keep your head
advancedExpressions.example: In the event of an earthquake, the first thing to do is to keep your head, take cover under a sturdy desk and wait for the shaking to stop. （安全须知,句型规范实用）

advancedExpressions.expression: it is those who keep their heads, not those who ..., that ...
advancedExpressions.example: It is those who keep their heads in the face of adversity, not those who are simply blessed with talent, that ultimately shape their own destiny.

sentenceUpgrade.original: She was scared but stayed calm.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Fear clutched at her chest and her legs threatened to give way, yet she kept her head, breathing slowly until her racing thoughts settled into a clear, deliberate plan. （读后续写·恐惧中的镇定）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Fear clutched at her chest 拟人化恐惧 + yet 转折凸显意志 + keep one's head 固定短语 + breathing slowly until... 分词+结果收束情绪

sentenceUpgrade.original: In difficult times we should not panic.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: History reminds us again and again that it is not brute strength but the capacity to keep one's head in the darkest hour that separates the truly great from the merely fortunate. （议论文·冷静的价值）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: History reminds us again and again 权威引入 + it is not... but... 强调句锁定重点 + keep one's head in the darkest hour 短语升级 + 对比收尾(the truly great / the merely fortunate)

translation: 宽慰，轻松；减轻，消除；救济
original_sentence: To her great relief, the officer immediately realized the coming danger.
readingExamples: To her great relief, the officer immediately realized the coming danger.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the pleasant feeling of relaxation and freedom from worry, pain or fear when something unpleasant stops or does not happen
(2) n. help, such as food, money or medical care, given to people in need after a disaster or in poverty
(3) n. the reduction or removal of pain, anxiety or a difficult situation
(4) n. (in art / geography) a way of carving or forming a design so that it stands out from a flat surface; the difference in height on a land surface

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 浮雕(艺术);(地表)起伏,地势
uncommonMeanings.example: Her fingertips traced the ancient stone relief on the temple wall, feeling the worn grooves where a thousand years of pilgrims had touched the same carved gods. （读后续写·古迹·历史厚重感）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 换班的人;替换者
uncommonMeanings.example: The exhausted guard glanced anxiously down the empty road, praying that his relief would arrive before the storm broke. （读后续写·值守·等待接班）

posExamples.sentence: When the doctor finally stepped out and said the operation had been a success, a wave of relief washed over the whole family, and the mother, who had not wept for hours, suddenly broke down in tears. （读后续写·手术·如释重负）
I am writing to appeal for your generous donations, for even a small sum can bring real relief to families whose homes were swept away by last month's floods. （应用文·募捐倡议）
True relief from stress comes not from escaping our responsibilities, but from facing them with a calmer, better-organised mind. （议论文·压力·心态）
To her great relief, the last bus had not yet left, and she sank into a seat by the window, letting out the breath she had been holding all the way from school. （读后续写·赶车·松一口气）

idioms.example: Much to his relief, the strict examiner smiled and nodded, and the tension that had gripped him all morning finally melted away. （读后续写·考试·紧张缓解）
Only when the ambulance doors closed safely behind them did the rescuers breathe a sigh of relief. （读后续写·救援·脱险）

idioms.idiom: a relief to do sth / that ...
idioms.example: It was such a relief to see the familiar lights of home glowing through the darkness after the long, frightening drive. （读后续写·归家·安心）

collocations.example: To her great relief, the officer immediately grasped the danger and ordered everyone to move to higher ground. （读后续写·预警·被理解）
A profound sense of relief settled over the exhausted climbers as the summit finally came into view. （读后续写·登顶·如释重负）
A wave of relief swept through the crowd the moment the missing child was carried out safely. （读后续写·寻回·群体情绪）
Volunteers from across the country rushed to join the flood relief, loading trucks with food, blankets and clean water. （应用文·志愿·救灾）
A short walk in the fresh air often brings surprising relief from the stress of a long day of study. （议论文/应用文·减压）

collocations.translation: 带来/提供缓解;提供救济
collocations.example: A single act of kindness can bring immense relief to someone quietly struggling under a heavy burden. （议论文·善意）
Unable to sleep, she sought relief in the pages of an old novel, and slowly the anxious hours slipped away. （读后续写·失眠·慰藉）
The relief efforts, though hampered by broken roads, gradually restored hope to the shattered mountain village. （应用文·救灾报道）
She read the message with relief, pressing the phone to her chest as if to make the good news last a little longer. （读后续写·收信·安心）

synonyms.example: In her darkest days, the quiet comfort of her grandmother's letters was the only thing that kept her going. （读后续写·慰藉·支撑）
synonyms.usage: comfort 侧重情感上的安慰、慰藉,可以是持续的;relief 侧重痛苦/担忧'解除后'那种轻松感,通常是瞬间的转变

synonyms.example: International aid poured into the earthquake-stricken region within hours of the first tremor. （应用文·救灾报道）
synonyms.usage: aid 泛指各种形式的帮助(物资、金钱、技术),范围最广;relief 特指灾后/困境中给予的紧急救济,情境更具体

synonyms.example: A single word of reassurance from the coach was enough to steady the nervous young player before the penalty. （读后续写·鼓励·安定人心）
synonyms.usage: reassurance 强调通过话语或行动'让人安心、消除疑虑';relief 是那种忧虑消除后自身感受到的轻松,主体不同

collocations.example: Despite the unbearable pain in his broken leg, he crawled inch by inch towards the flickering light of the rescue lamp. （读后续写·求生·意志）
The unbearable heat of the noonday sun beat down on the marchers, yet not one of them was willing to be the first to stop. （读后续写·坚持）
As hour after hour passed with no news, the waiting grew unbearable, and every ring of the telephone made my heart leap. （读后续写·焦急等待）

collocations.translation: 刺眼得令人难受的强光
collocations.example: For a heartbeat the fire burnt with an unbearable light, so fierce that the onlookers flung up their hands to shield their eyes. （读后续写·灾难·感官冲击）
An unbearable silence settled over the classroom as the teacher slowly unfolded the results of the final exam. （读后续写·紧张氛围）
She found the thought of leaving her students unbearable, and for the first time in years her eyes brimmed with tears. （读后续写·师生情）
The suspense during the final minute of the match was almost unbearable, and the whole stadium seemed to hold its breath. （读后续写·比赛·紧张）

synonyms.translation: 无法容忍的，不能接受的
synonyms.example: The committee agreed that such unfair treatment of volunteers was simply intolerable and must be corrected at once. （应用文/议论文·正式）
synonyms.usage: intolerable 更正式，多指道德或原则上'不能容忍'的行为、状况；unbearable 更常指感官或情感上'受不了'的痛苦、炎热、寂静等。

synonyms.example: Hour after hour in the freezing water, his exhaustion became unendurable, and yet the thought of his waiting family kept him afloat. （读后续写·极限）
synonyms.usage: unendurable 与 unbearable 意思极近，但更书面、程度更重，强调'再也撑不下去'；日常写作 unbearable 更通用自然。

synonyms.example: The room was unbearably hot, and beads of sweat trickled down every anxious face. （读后续写·环境）
synonyms.usage: 副词形式，直接修饰形容词/动词，比'unbearable + 名词'更精炼有力，适合快速渲染程度。

advancedExpressions.expression: ..., the ... had become unbearable, and ...
advancedExpressions.example: As the minutes dragged on, the suspense had become unbearable, and I could feel my heart pounding against my ribs. （用 unbearable 顶点化情绪 + and 引出生理反应，虚实结合渲染紧张）

advancedExpressions.expression: the ... has grown unbearable; we therefore urge ...
advancedExpressions.example: The noise from the construction site has grown almost unbearable for students in the reading room; we therefore urge the authorities to take immediate action. （先陈述问题严重性，再顺势提出诉求）

advancedExpressions.expression: what once seemed unbearable often ...
advancedExpressions.example: What once seemed unbearable often turns out, in hindsight, to be the very trial that shapes our character and steels our resolve.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The pain was too much to stand.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The pain shooting up his arm was almost unbearable, yet he clenched his teeth, refusing to cry out and betray the fear that gripped his heart. （读后续写·忍痛·意志）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: shooting up his arm 现在分词描摹痛感走向 + almost unbearable 程度递进 + yet 转折凸显意志 + clenched his teeth 动作细节外化坚忍。

sentenceUpgrade.original: It was very hot in the room and everyone was uncomfortable.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The heat inside the crowded hall had grown so unbearable that the air itself seemed to press down on us, and one by one the weary faces began to glisten with sweat. （读后续写·环境·群像）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: so unbearable that... so...that 结果句 + the air seemed to press down 拟人夸张 + one by one... 群像细节，把抽象的'热'转化为可感画面。

original_sentence: The cries of women broke out; the men looked at each other, but were silent.
readingExamples: The cries of women broke out; the men looked at each other, but were silent.
definitionEn:
(1) v. (of war, fighting, disease, fire, etc.) to begin suddenly
(2) v. to escape from a place, especially a prison
(3) v. (of an unpleasant physical condition) to appear suddenly on the skin
(4) v. break out in / into — to suddenly start sweating, laughing, singing, etc.

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （皮肤上）突然长出（疹子、汗珠等）
uncommonMeanings.example: The instant the examiner called his name, cold sweat broke out on his forehead, and his carefully rehearsed lines dissolved into a blur. （读后续写·紧张时刻·生理反应）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （从监禁或困境中）逃脱，挣脱
uncommonMeanings.example: For three long years he had dreamed of the moment he would break out of that grey, suffocating routine and finally chase the life he truly wanted. （读后续写·人物觉醒·摆脱束缚）

posExamples.sentence: A deafening cheer broke out across the stadium the second the whistle blew, and strangers who had never spoken were suddenly hugging one another like lifelong friends. （读后续写·比赛胜利·群体欢腾）
I am writing to remind every resident that, should a fire break out in the building, you must remain calm, use the staircase rather than the lift, and gather at the assigned meeting point. （应用文·通知）
History teaches us that wars rarely break out overnight; more often they smoulder for years, fed by mistrust and injustice, until a single spark sets the whole region ablaze. （议论文·历史与和平）
No sooner had the teacher stepped out of the classroom than a fierce argument broke out between the two boys over the borrowed dictionary. （读后续写·校园冲突）

idioms.idiom: break out in a cold sweat
idioms.example: When the headlights suddenly swung towards her on the dark road, she broke out in a cold sweat and froze where she stood. （读后续写·惊恐时刻）

collocations.example: When war broke out, the once-bustling town emptied overnight, its windows shuttered and its streets swallowed by an uneasy silence. （读后续写·战乱背景）
Should a fire break out during the exhibition, staff will guide visitors calmly towards the nearest emergency exit. （应用文·安全须知）

collocations.phrase: a disease / an epidemic breaks out
collocations.example: The moment a mysterious disease broke out in the village, the young doctor cancelled his leave and rushed back without a second thought. （读后续写·奉献精神）

collocations.phrase: an argument / a quarrel breaks out
collocations.example: A heated argument broke out among the volunteers over how the limited donations should be shared. （应用文·活动记述）
As the lights went out and the ground trembled, panic broke out and the crowd surged towards the doors. （读后续写·灾难现场）
The film tells the gripping story of a wrongly convicted man who spends a decade plotting to break out of prison. （读后续写·电影梗概）
Within minutes of touching the plant, her arms broke out in an angry red rash. （读后续写·意外插曲）

collocations.translation: 突然大笑 / 唱起歌来
collocations.example: The whole coach broke out into song as the tour bus wound its way up the misty mountain road. （读后续写·旅途温情）

synonyms.example: Cheers erupted from the audience the moment the little-known performer hit the final, soaring note. （读后续写·舞台高潮）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:erupt 强调像火山一样猛烈、突然地喷发，语气比 break out 更强烈，多用于欢呼、掌声、暴力、火山等；break out 更中性通用。

synonyms.example: Unable to hold it in any longer, she burst out crying in the middle of the crowded hall. （读后续写·情感失控）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:burst out 后接动名词或引语，专指情绪/声音的突然迸发（burst out laughing/crying）；break out 侧重事件（战争、火灾、疾病）的突然开始。

synonyms.example: Old tensions flared up again the instant the two rivals were seated at the same table. （读后续写·旧怨重燃）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:flare up 强调本已存在的矛盾/病情突然加剧、复燃；break out 更强调从无到有地开始。

advancedExpressions.expression: no sooner had ... than ... broke out
advancedExpressions.example: No sooner had the last note faded than thunderous applause broke out, washing over the trembling boy like a warm tide. （倒装+比喻,续写高潮段）

advancedExpressions.expression: in the event that a fire / an emergency breaks out, one should ...
advancedExpressions.example: In the event that a fire breaks out, you are strongly advised to keep calm and follow the marked evacuation route. （通知/须知的规范提醒句式）

advancedExpressions.expression: conflicts break out not because of ... but because of ...
advancedExpressions.example: Conflicts break out not because differences exist, but because we fail to understand and respect them — and therein lies the true value of communication.

sentenceUpgrade.original: Then everyone started shouting happily.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Then, as if a dam had burst, a wave of joyful shouting broke out across the square, and the tears people had held back all day finally streamed freely down their faces. （读后续写·群体欢庆）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: as if a dam had burst 虚拟比喻 + broke out 精准动词 + 补充细节(tears streamed)营造画面感

sentenceUpgrade.original: If a fire happens, leave the building quickly.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Should a fire break out, all residents are kindly requested to evacuate the building via the nearest staircase in an orderly manner. （应用文·通知）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Should 引导的倒装虚拟条件句 + break out 地道搭配 + are requested to 正式被动礼貌语气

translation: adv. 在（或向）较远处，在另一边 | prep. 在（或向）更远处；超出；晚于；无法；超出…之外
original_sentence: At that moment, they felt the earth shaking beneath their feet; beyond in the distance, they heard the crash of falling roofs.
readingExamples: At that moment, they felt the earth shaking beneath their feet; beyond in the distance, they heard the crash of falling roofs.
definitionEn:
(1) prep. on or to the further side of something; farther away than something
(2) prep. later than a particular time; after
(3) prep. more than a particular amount, level, or limit
(4) adv. on or to the further side; farther on
(5) prep. too difficult or impossible for someone to do, understand, or imagine

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （能力、理解、可能性）超出……之外，非……所能
uncommonMeanings.example: As she watched the frail old man carry the drowning child to safety, she realised his courage was beyond anything she could ever put into words. （读后续写·情感升华·无法言表）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （the beyond）远方；来世，彼岸（文学用法）
uncommonMeanings.example: He gazed out at the endless dunes, half-expecting some answer to drift back to him from the silent beyond. （读后续写·苍凉意境）

posExamples.sentence: Beyond the crumbling stone wall lay a secret garden, its roses running wild, as if time itself had forgotten to pass in that forgotten corner of the world. （读后续写·环境描写·秘境）
I would like to remind all participants that the library will remain open beyond its usual hours during the final examination week, closing at eleven each evening. （应用文·通知）
True education must reach beyond the mere transmission of knowledge; it should awaken curiosity, cultivate character, and prepare young people to think for themselves. （议论文·教育本质）
She climbed to the very top of the hill, and there, stretching far beyond, lay a shimmering sea she had only ever seen in her dreams. （读后续写·豁然开朗·希望）

idioms.example: His unwavering dedication over those ten long years proved beyond doubt that talent means little without perseverance. （议论文·坚持的力量）
The view from the summit at dawn was beyond compare, and for a long moment none of us dared to break the silence. （读后续写·壮丽景色）

idioms.translation: 远超某人最疯狂的梦想
idioms.example: To stand on that podium, a medal round her neck, was a triumph beyond her wildest dreams. （读后续写·梦想成真）

collocations.example: For years a university education had seemed forever beyond her reach, until a kind stranger offered to pay her tuition. （读后续写·改变命运）
Due to circumstances beyond our control, the outdoor charity fair has been postponed to next Saturday. （应用文·通知）
The kindness the villagers showed us during the storm was beyond words, and we left with our hearts full and our eyes wet. （读后续写·感恩）
It is beyond question that regular exercise benefits both body and mind. （议论文·健康观点）
The ancient bridge, battered by the flood, was damaged beyond repair, and the whole town mourned its loss. （读后续写·失去）
That a boy so young could compose such music was, to the audience, almost beyond belief. （读后续写·惊叹）
A good volunteer always goes beyond what is asked, offering not just help but warmth and dignity. （议论文·奉献精神）
By the time help arrived, he was exhausted beyond the point of standing, yet he refused to let go of the rope. （读后续写·极限坚持）

synonyms.example: She hurried past the old oak tree and did not slow down until the frightening shadows were far behind her. （读后续写·紧张逃离）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:past 侧重从某物旁边经过或时间已过；beyond 强调在更远的另一侧，或超出限度/理解，语义范围更广、更书面。

synonyms.example: Her performance surpassed everyone's expectations, silencing even her harshest critics. （读后续写·惊艳全场）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:surpass 是及物动词，强调在质量/程度上胜过某标准；beyond 是介词/副词，构成 beyond expectations 等短语，用法更灵活。

synonyms.example: The braver we grow, the further we dare to venture into the unknown. （议论文·勇气）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:farther/further 是副词，单纯表示距离更远；beyond 兼作介词，可引出具体对象(beyond the hill)，还能表抽象的“超出”。

advancedExpressions.expression: what happened next was beyond anything sb. had ever imagined
advancedExpressions.example: What happened next was beyond anything she had ever imagined: the crowd rose to its feet as one, and the applause seemed to lift the very roof. （悬念铺垫+情感放大,续写转折段）

advancedExpressions.expression: due to circumstances beyond our control, ...
advancedExpressions.example: Due to circumstances beyond our control, the departure time has been moved beyond nine o'clock; we sincerely apologise for any inconvenience. （通知中说明客观原因的礼貌套路）

advancedExpressions.expression: the significance of ... extends far beyond ...
advancedExpressions.example: The significance of reading extends far beyond passing examinations; it shapes how we see the world and who we choose to become.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The mountains were very far away.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Far beyond the misty valley, the mountains rose one behind another, fading from deep green to a pale, dreamlike blue at the very edge of the sky. （读后续写·远景描写）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Far beyond 引导地点状语前置 + 色彩递进(deep green→pale blue) + 视觉纵深感营造画面

sentenceUpgrade.original: This problem is too hard for me to solve.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: I must admit, in all honesty, that a challenge of this magnitude lies entirely beyond my present capabilities. （应用文·正式书信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: I must admit in all honesty 插入语提升语气 + of this magnitude 正式搭配 + lies beyond one's capabilities 书面表达

translation: 遥远，久远；距离；差异；疏远
original_sentence: At that moment, they felt the earth shaking beneath their feet; beyond in the distance, they heard the crash of falling roofs.
readingExamples: At that moment, they felt the earth shaking beneath their feet; beyond in the distance, they heard the crash of falling roofs.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the amount of space between two places or things
(2) n. a place or point that is far away from someone or something (often 'in the distance', 'from a distance')
(3) n. the state of being far away in space or time
(4) n. a feeling that you are not friendly with someone or not emotionally involved with them; reserve

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （情感上的）疏远，冷淡
uncommonMeanings.example: Ever since the quarrel, a quiet distance had grown between father and son, and the dinner table, once full of laughter, now echoed with an awkward silence. （读后续写·亲情裂痕）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: distance oneself from — 使自己与……保持距离，疏远
uncommonMeanings.example: As the rumours spread, one by one his so-called friends began to distance themselves from him, leaving him to face the storm alone. （读后续写·孤立无援）

posExamples.sentence: In the distance, a single lantern glowed against the darkness, and the lost traveller's heart leapt with hope as he stumbled towards that fragile promise of shelter. （读后续写·绝境中的希望）
I am writing to inform you that, given the considerable distance between the campsite and the nearest town, all participants should bring enough food and water for two full days. （应用文·通知）
Distance, far from weakening true friendship, often deepens it, for it teaches us to treasure what we can no longer take for granted. （议论文·友谊的距离）
She could still make out his figure in the distance, growing smaller and fainter, until at last the crowd swallowed him and he was gone. （读后续写·离别不舍）

idioms.example: Many joined the training full of enthusiasm, but only those with real grit went the distance and stood at the finish line. （读后续写·坚持到底）

idioms.translation: 对某人保持距离，不亲近
idioms.example: Wounded by past betrayals, she instinctively kept everyone at a distance, hiding her loneliness behind a polite smile. （读后续写·内心防备）

collocations.example: In the distance, thunder rumbled and the first heavy drops began to fall on the parched fields. （读后续写·环境铺垫）
From a distance the old house looked grand, but up close its peeling paint told a very different story. （读后续写·今昔对比）
The lighthouse can be seen at a distance of nearly twenty kilometres on a clear night. （应用文·景点介绍）
The wild deer kept its distance, watching us with wary, glistening eyes. （读后续写·人与自然）
Having covered a great distance on foot, the weary hikers finally caught sight of the shelter. （读后续写·长途跋涉）
The dormitory is conveniently located within walking distance of both the library and the canteen. （应用文·校园介绍）
A responsible citizen should firmly distance himself from any behaviour that harms the public interest. （议论文·公民责任）
Please keep a safe distance from the platform edge while the train is approaching. （应用文·安全提示）

synonyms.example: The teacher's patient guidance gradually bridged the gap between the shy boy and his more confident classmates. （读后续写·成长跨越）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:gap 强调两者之间的空缺、差距（贫富差距、代沟），可抽象可具体；distance 更强调可测量的空间距离，或情感疏远。

synonyms.example: She asked for a little space to think things through before making such an important decision. （读后续写·独处思考）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:space 侧重可用的空间或（情感上）需要的独处余地；distance 强调两点之间的“远”。give sb. space 意为给某人空间，不能换成 distance。

synonyms.example: The signal is strong only within a limited range of the tower. （议论文/说明文·技术）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:range 强调有效范围、幅度（射程、音域、价格区间）；distance 单纯指两点间的距离长度。

advancedExpressions.expression: in the distance, sb. could just make out ...
advancedExpressions.example: In the distance, through the swirling snow, she could just make out the faint outline of a cottage — and with it, a flicker of hope. （远景+希望意象,续写转折段）

advancedExpressions.expression: given the distance between ... and ..., it is advisable to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Given the considerable distance between the venue and the station, it is advisable to set out at least an hour in advance. （通知/提醒的规范说明句式）

advancedExpressions.expression: distance does not divide us; rather, it ...
advancedExpressions.example: Distance does not divide us; rather, it reminds us how deeply we are connected, and how much a single message can mean across a thousand miles.

sentenceUpgrade.original: She saw a light far away and felt hopeful.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Far off in the distance, a solitary light trembled in the darkness, and at the sight of it something long frozen in her chest began, ever so slightly, to thaw. （读后续写·希望重燃）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: in the distance 远景意象 + 拟物(a light trembled) + 心理隐喻(something frozen began to thaw)表达希望

sentenceUpgrade.original: The two towns are far from each other.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Separated by a considerable distance, the two towns had, over the centuries, developed customs so different that a visitor might well feel he had crossed into another country. （议论文/说明文·文化差异）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 过去分词短语 Separated by 开头 + a considerable distance 正式搭配 + so...that 结果状语从句增强论证

original_sentence: Over the empty streets—over the forum—far and wide—with many a noisy crash in the stormy sea—fell that awful shower!
readingExamples: Over the empty streets—over the forum—far and wide—with many a noisy crash in the stormy sea—fell that awful shower!
definitionEn:
(1) adv. over a large area; in or to many places
(2) adv. (often with 'search', 'travel', 'known') everywhere; to or from all directions

posExamples.sentence: News of the young hero's bravery spread far and wide, and before long strangers were travelling for miles just to shake his hand. （读后续写·英雄事迹传扬）
We are proud to announce that our school choir is now known far and wide, having won first prize in three provincial competitions this year alone. （应用文·喜报/广播稿）
A truly good idea, once shared, travels far and wide, crossing borders and generations to enrich minds its creator will never meet. （议论文·思想的传播）
The frantic villagers searched far and wide for the missing child, their lanterns bobbing like fireflies across the darkened hills. （读后续写·全村寻人）

idioms.example: He searched far and wide for a teacher who could truly understand him, and at last, in the quietest corner of the town, he found her. （读后续写·寻觅良师）

idioms.idiom: far and wide known / known far and wide
idioms.example: Her selfless devotion to the orphans made her known far and wide as the 'mother of a hundred children'. （读后续写·美德传扬）

collocations.example: Once posted online, the touching video spread far and wide, moving millions to tears within a single day. （应用文·新闻报道）
Having travelled far and wide, the old sailor had a thousand tales to tell, each stranger than the last. （读后续写·阅历丰富）
They searched far and wide for volunteers willing to give up their holidays for the flood relief. （应用文·招募）
The little bakery was known far and wide for the warm bread it handed out free to anyone in need. （读后续写·善举远播）
On the festival morning, crowds came from far and wide to witness the ancient ceremony. （读后续写·节日盛况）

synonyms.example: News of the rescue was everywhere the next morning, splashed across every front page in the country. （应用文·新闻）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:everywhere 最普通、口语化，泛指“各处”；far and wide 更书面、更有文学色彩，强调“广远、遍及各方”，多与 spread/search/known 搭配。

synonyms.example: After the storm, broken branches lay all over the place, and it took the whole community a week to clear them. （读后续写·灾后）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:all over the place 口语随意，还可引申为“乱七八糟”；far and wide 语气庄重，多用于传播、寻找、闻名等正面语境。

synonyms.example: She hunted high and low for the lost letter, turning every drawer inside out. （读后续写·翻找）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:high and low 也是固定短语，专指“上上下下、到处找”，几乎只与 search/hunt/look 连用；far and wide 覆盖范围更广，含义更宽。

advancedExpressions.expression: word of ... spread far and wide, until ...
advancedExpressions.example: Word of his kindness spread far and wide, until the once-forgotten village became a place people travelled miles to see. （从传播到结果的递进,续写升华段）

advancedExpressions.expression: we sincerely hope this message will spread far and wide
advancedExpressions.example: We sincerely hope this message will spread far and wide, so that every corner of our campus may share in the joy of reading. （倡议/广播稿的扩散号召）

advancedExpressions.expression: the influence of ... reaches far and wide, touching ...

synonyms.usage: 专指数量、程度或坡度的陡急变化，可与 sharp rise/fall 互换；但 steep 不能表"锋利"或"敏锐"

synonyms.example: The music came to an abrupt stop, and every dancer froze mid-step as if turned to stone. （读后续写·戏剧转折）
synonyms.usage: 强调"突然、意外、缺乏过渡"，也可指言行唐突无礼；sharp 侧重变化的"剧烈幅度"而非纯粹的"突然"

advancedExpressions.expression: a sharp ... cut through the ... , as if ...
advancedExpressions.example: A sharp cry cut through the midnight silence, as if the very darkness had been torn open. （感官动词 cut through + as if 比喻，用声音撕裂静默制造惊悚氛围）

advancedExpressions.expression: as the figures reveal, there has been a sharp ... in ...
advancedExpressions.example: As the figures reveal, there has been a sharp increase in the number of students cycling to school, a heartening sign of growing green awareness. （as...reveal 引数据 + sharp increase 描述趋势，报告类应用文高分句式）

advancedExpressions.expression: in sharp contrast to ..., ...
advancedExpressions.example: In sharp contrast to those who wait passively for luck, achievers sharpen their skills day after day until opportunity, when it finally comes, finds them ready. （in sharp contrast to 引出对立面，凸显立场）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The dog has a good sense of smell and found the man quickly.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Guided by a sense of smell so sharp that no scent could escape it, the search dog wove through the rubble and, with a triumphant bark, pinpointed the buried survivor within minutes. （读后续写·搜救犬·画面）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 过去分词状语开头(Guided by...)交代方式 + so...that 强调嗅觉之灵敏 + 动作动词(wove, pinpointed)增强画面 + triumphant 情感副词渲染

sentenceUpgrade.original: The number of readers dropped a lot this term.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: This term has witnessed a sharp decline in the number of readers, a worrying trend that urgently calls for our collective attention and action. （应用文·倡议信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 拟人主语(This term has witnessed)提升正式度 + sharp decline 精准描述趋势 + 同位语(a worrying trend that...)补充评价并引出呼吁

translation: 找出…的准确位置；把…安置在（或建造于）
original_sentence: Because of their small size and sharp sense of smell, dogs can locate survivors much faster than humans can.
readingExamples: Because of their small size and sharp sense of smell, dogs can locate survivors much faster than humans can.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to find the exact position or place of someone or something
(2) vt. to put or build something in a particular place; to situate
(3) vi. to move to and start a business or home in a new place; to settle
(4) vt. (be located) to be situated in a particular position or place

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 确定（问题、根源、责任等）的所在，找出症结
uncommonMeanings.example: Only after hours of patient questioning did the counsellor manage to locate the real source of the boy's silence — not laziness, but a fear of failing those he loved. （读后续写·心理疏导·探寻根源）

posExamples.sentence: Because of their small size and sharp sense of smell, dogs can locate survivors much faster than humans can, weaving through gaps too narrow for any rescuer to follow. （读后续写·搜救犬·能力）
I would suggest that the new reading corner be located near the sunny windows, where soft natural light can make every quiet afternoon of reading a genuine pleasure. （应用文·建议信）
Before rushing to blame students for their poor grades, wise teachers first try to locate the underlying cause, for a symptom treated without diagnosis is rarely cured. （议论文·教育反思）
Fumbling in the pitch-black tent, she finally located the torch, and its trembling beam brought a small circle of comfort to the endless mountain night. （读后续写·野外求生·摸索）

wordForms.other: relocate (vt. 重新安置，迁移); dislocate (vt. 使脱臼；扰乱)

collocations.example: Using only the faint signal from her phone, the rescue team managed to locate the lost hiker before nightfall swallowed the valley. （读后续写·山野救援）

collocations.phrase: be located in / on / at / near
collocations.example: Our school is located at the foot of a green hill, where birdsong drifts through the classroom windows every spring morning. （应用文·学校介绍）

collocations.translation: 找出根源 / 原因 / 问题所在
collocations.example: The engineers worked through the night to locate the source of the leak, tracing it at last to a single cracked valve deep within the plant. （读后续写·排查故障）

collocations.phrase: locate survivors / a target / a fault
collocations.translation: 定位幸存者 / 目标 / 故障
collocations.example: Thermal cameras helped the crew locate survivors trapped beneath the snow, each glowing dot on the screen a heartbeat still fighting on. （读后续写·雪崩搜救）
The hidden spring was hard to locate, yet the villagers' faith in the old map never wavered as they climbed higher into the mist. （读后续写·寻访探索）

collocations.translation: 位置便利 / 位于中心地带
collocations.example: The new youth centre is conveniently located beside the subway station, making it easy for students from every district to join our weekend activities. （应用文·活动通知）

collocations.phrase: locate a company / factory / office (in a place)
collocations.translation: 把公司（工厂、办公室）设在……
collocations.example: The firm chose to locate its research base in our city, drawn by its clean air, low costs and steady supply of talented graduates. （议论文·城市发展）

synonyms.example: After searching every drawer, she finally found the faded photograph that held the last trace of her grandmother's smile. （读后续写·寻物动情）
synonyms.usage: 最通用、最口语的词，泛指找到任何东西；locate 更正式、更强调"确定精确位置"，多用于科技、救援、地理语境

synonyms.example: The temple is situated on a lonely cliff, its bell echoing across the valley at dawn. （读后续写·景物描写）
synonyms.usage: 几乎只用于"位于某处"的静态含义(be situated)，与 be located 同义；但 situate 不用于"寻找、定位"这一动态含义

synonyms.example: The doctors could not pinpoint the exact cause of the fever, yet they never stopped searching for answers. （议论文·科学探究）
synonyms.usage: 强调"精确到点"的定位，比 locate 更突出准确性，常用于找出确切位置或原因，语气更精细

synonyms.example: Detectives traced the anonymous letter to a quiet flat on the edge of town. （读后续写·侦探追查）
synonyms.usage: 强调"顺着线索一步步追查"的过程，隐含追溯来源或去向；locate 只强调最终确定位置，不含追溯过程

advancedExpressions.expression: no matter how ..., sb. was determined to locate ...
advancedExpressions.example: No matter how thick the fog grew or how numb her fingers became, she was determined to locate the lost child before the mountain surrendered to night. （no matter how 让步 + be determined to 决心，塑造搜救者的执着）

advancedExpressions.expression: conveniently located just ... away from ..., ... offers ...
advancedExpressions.example: Conveniently located just a short walk away from the station, our library offers a peaceful haven for anyone longing to lose themselves in a good book. （过去分词短语前置 + offer 引出优势，介绍类应用文高分开头）

advancedExpressions.expression: the first step towards solving ... is to locate its root cause
advancedExpressions.example: The first step towards solving any social problem is to locate its root cause; treating the surface while ignoring the origin only breeds fresh troubles tomorrow. （the first step is to... 结构 + 分号对比，逻辑清晰的论证句）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The dogs found the survivors quickly.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Noses low to the shattered ground, the dogs threaded through the ruins and located the survivors far faster than any human searcher could, each urgent bark rekindling a spark of hope in the watching crowd. （读后续写·搜救犬·画面）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 分词状语开头(Noses low to...)聚焦细节 + 动词连缀(threaded, located)推进 + 比较结构(far faster than...) + 结尾意象(spark of hope)升华情感

sentenceUpgrade.original: The new library is in a good place near the station.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Ideally located just minutes from the station, the new library stands as a welcoming sanctuary where knowledge and quiet await every curious visitor. （应用文·场所介绍）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 过去分词短语前置(Ideally located...)提升句式 + stand as 隐喻(sanctuary) + where 定语从句渲染氛围

original_sentence: In that case, they have to retire.
readingExamples: In that case, they have to retire.
definitionEn:
(1) vi. to stop working, usually because you have reached a certain age
(2) vt. to make an employee stop working, especially by giving them a pension
(3) vi. to leave a competition, game or activity before it is finished, often because of injury
(4) vi. (formal) to go away to a quiet or private place, especially to bed or to rest

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （正式）就寝，退下，退到僻静处（并非退休，而是"回房休息"）
uncommonMeanings.example: Long after the guests had retired for the night, the old innkeeper sat alone by the dying fire, turning a faded letter over and over in his weathered hands. （读后续写·夜深独处·氛围渲染）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （因伤病或状态不佳）中途退赛，退出比赛
uncommonMeanings.example: With his ankle twisted and his dream of gold slipping away, the marathon runner was forced to retire, yet the applause that met him rang louder than any medal. （读后续写·体育赛场·遗憾中的尊严）

posExamples.sentence: When a search dog can no longer keep pace with the young ones, its handler knows that, in that case, the loyal companion has to retire, and a quieter life of grass and sunshine begins. （读后续写·搜救犬·功成身退）
I am writing to invite you to the farewell party for Mr Li, who will retire this summer after devoting thirty selfless years to our school. （应用文·邀请信）
Some argue that people should retire early to enjoy life, yet others insist that meaningful work, far from wearing us down, is precisely what keeps the mind young and the spirit alive. （议论文·观点论证）
On the day my grandfather finally retired, he hung his worn tools on the wall like old friends, and for the first time in forty years the workshop fell silent. （读后续写·退休感怀·画面）

wordForms.other: retirement (n. 退休；退休生活)

idioms.translation: 退出（活动、公共生活等）舞台，隐退
idioms.example: After one last dazzling performance, the ageing violinist chose to retire from the stage, leaving the audience on their feet and their eyes brimming with tears. （读后续写·艺术生涯·谢幕）

collocations.phrase: retire from (a job / the army / politics)
collocations.translation: 从（工作、军队、政界）退休（退役、引退）
collocations.example: When the old general retired from the army, he traded his medals for a hoe and spent his final years coaxing roses from the barren hillside. （读后续写·退役人生·转变）

collocations.translation: 以（教师、主管）的身份退休
collocations.example: She retired as headmistress last June, yet hardly a week passes without a former pupil knocking at her door to share good news. （读后续写·师恩绵长）
My grandfather retired at the age of sixty, but his passion for teaching burned on, and soon a free evening class filled our tiny living room. （读后续写·退而不休）
Rather than retire early and drift into idleness, he stayed on, mentoring a new generation of engineers with tireless patience. （议论文·奉献精神）

collocations.phrase: retire for the night / to bed
collocations.example: The storm raged on as the family retired for the night, each of them listening, wide-eyed, to the rain lashing against the shutters. （读后续写·雨夜就寝）
Injured in the semi-final, the captain was forced to retire, yet from the sidelines his roaring encouragement drove his teammates to victory. （读后续写·带伤退赛·团队精神）

collocations.translation: 退休教师 / 退伍军人 / 退休工人
collocations.example: A retired teacher in our neighbourhood opens her tiny library every weekend, and children flock to it as bees to a blossom. （读后续写·社区温情）
After decades of honest toil, the old couple could at last retire in peace, watching their grandchildren grow beneath the pear tree they had planted together. （读后续写·晚年安宁）

synonyms.example: Unwilling to compromise his principles, the young manager chose to resign rather than sign the dishonest report. （议论文·坚守原则）
synonyms.usage: 指主动"辞去"某一职位，通常出于个人意愿且与年龄无关；retire 特指因到年龄而"退休"，多为职业生涯的自然终点

synonyms.example: Overwhelmed by nerves, she almost withdrew from the contest, until her coach's quiet words steadied her trembling hands. （读后续写·临阵退缩）
synonyms.usage: 泛指"退出"活动、比赛、协议或撤回言论，语域广而中性；retire from a competition 特指因伤病等中途退赛，且 retire 还有"退休、就寝"等义

synonyms.example: After leading the club to three championships, the veteran coach decided to step down and let a younger mind take the helm. （应用文·致辞/读后续写·交棒）
synonyms.usage: 指从领导岗位、要职上"卸任、让位"，强调主动交出权力；retire 更侧重整个职业生涯的结束，未必涉及权力交接

synonyms.example: As the flood rose, the villagers were forced to retreat to the higher ground, carrying their frightened children on their backs. （读后续写·灾难撤离）
synonyms.usage: 本义为"（军事上）撤退"或从危险、困境中"退避"，也可指隐居；retire 无"撤离危险"之义，两者仅在"退到僻静处"这一冷僻义上偶有交叠

advancedExpressions.expression: though sb. had retired, ...
advancedExpressions.example: Though he had retired years ago, the old fireman's heart never truly left the station, and at the first wail of a distant siren he would rise, as if the bell still called his name. （though 让步从句 + as if 虚拟，刻画退休者不灭的初心）

advancedExpressions.expression: as sb. retires after ... years of devotion, we ...
advancedExpressions.example: As Mr Wang retires after forty years of devotion to this school, we wish to convey our deepest gratitude for the countless lives he has quietly shaped. （as 引出背景 + convey gratitude 正式致谢，欢送信升华句）

advancedExpressions.expression: to retire is not to ..., but to ...
advancedExpressions.example: To retire is not to fade quietly from the world, but to open a new chapter in which experience becomes wisdom and free hours become a gift to others. （not to...but to... 平行否定升华，重新定义"退休"的意义）

sentenceUpgrade.original: After many years of work, the old dog had to retire.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: After years of faithful service, its once-tireless legs now trembling on the stairs, the old search dog had to retire at last, curling up in the sunlit corner it had earned through a lifetime of courage. （读后续写·搜救犬·功成身退）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 独立主格结构(its legs now trembling)补充状态 + at last 强化情感 + 结尾意象(sunlit corner...earned through a lifetime of courage)升华，赋予退休以尊严

sentenceUpgrade.original: Our teacher will retire this year, so we want to thank him.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: As our beloved teacher prepares to retire this year, we feel compelled to express our profound gratitude for the seeds of knowledge and kindness he has patiently sown in every one of us. （应用文·感谢/欢送信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: as 时间状语从句铺陈背景 + feel compelled to 正式表达强烈情感 + 隐喻(seeds of knowledge and kindness...sown)增强感染力
